elements.element: Vendor is the indemnifying party and owes a duty to defend.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Vendor “shall defend” against covered claims.

elements.element: Vendor owes a duty to indemnify for resulting damages, liabilities, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Vendor to “indemnify and hold harmless” and expressly covers these resulting losses.

elements.element: Customer and its Affiliates are protected beneficiaries of Vendor's indemnity.
elements.evidence: The protected parties are expressly “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity applies to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The opening language applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights, without the fallback exclusions.
elements.evidence: Although paragraph (a) covers allegations involving the Services and Deliverables, the next paragraph excludes claims arising from specified Customer modifications, combinations, and specifications. Those exclusions are expressly part of the fallback position, not the preferred position.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) covers “Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly covers “Vendor's gross negligence.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (d) expressly covers “wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires prompt notice and excuses performance for delayed notice only to the extent of resulting prejudice.
elements.evidence: The procedure requires prompt written notice and states that delay excuses the indemnifying party only to the extent prejudiced.

elements.element: The indemnifying party controls the defence.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly gives the indemnifying party control of the defence and settlement.

elements.element: Settlement control is subject to customary protections for the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: Without written consent, the indemnifying party may not admit liability, impose a non-monetary obligation, or enter a settlement that fails to release the indemnified party.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity exposure for Customer-provided content is limited to third-party claims arising from content or materials supplied by Customer.
elements.evidence: Customer indemnifies only for third-party claims arising from content or materials provided by Customer, with an additional Customer-favorable exception for Customer Data processed as contemplated.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity exposure includes only Customer's breach of law as the other permitted trigger.
elements.evidence: The only other stated trigger is “Customer's breach of Applicable Law.”

elements.element: Customer has no indemnification obligations beyond the stated Customer-content and breach-of-law indemnities.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states, “This is Customer's only indemnity under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Vendor provides an IP indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights.
elements.evidence: The first indemnity paragraph covers allegations involving the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology and includes defence and indemnification.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The exclusion applies to Customer modifications made without Vendor's authorization.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by combinations with other items.
elements.evidence: The exclusion covers combinations with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided without the combination.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The exclusion covers Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

elements.element: The IP remedies are triggered when an IP claim arises or is reasonably likely and are provided at Vendor's expense.
elements.evidence: The remedies paragraph applies if the specified claim “arises or is reasonably likely” and requires Vendor to act “at its expense.”

elements.element: Vendor must offer to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: Procurement of continued-use rights is expressly one of Customer's options.

elements.element: Vendor must offer to modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing while remaining functionally equivalent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly offers modification to a “functionally equivalent non-infringing item.”

elements.element: Vendor must offer to replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: Replacement with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item is expressly offered.

elements.element: If the continued-use, modification, or replacement remedies are not reasonably available, Customer receives an appropriate refund.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate affected items and receive prepaid Fees for terminated items plus Fees paid for Deliverables it can no longer use.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability is subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees cap appears. Section 21.3 instead classifies indemnification obligations as “Excluded Claims,” with no operative super-cap supplied.

result.reason: The language supplies nearly all preferred indemnity triggers, procedures, and the narrow Customer indemnity, but it does not achieve the preferred position because it adds the IP exclusions reserved for fallback. It also fails fallback because there is no 3× annual-fees super-cap. The draft is therefore an incomplete hybrid rather than a complete playbook level. Unrelated commercial terms remain substantively intact, but drafting quality is materially reduced because the inserted paragraphs are unnumbered while repeatedly referring to Sections 20.1(a) and 20.5, and the remedies paragraph says “neither remedy” after listing three alternatives.
